newsitem.title: CANADA: CANFAX analyst sees Canada beef output up in 1997.
newsitem.headline: CANFAX analyst sees Canada beef output up in 1997.

text.p: Canadian beef production will rise 3.5 percent to 3.207 billion lbs in 1997 before falling off annually through the year 2000, CANFAX cattle analyst, Anne Dunford said.

"For 1997, herd liquidation will continue. Beef production should peak. Cattle prices should improve in the second half of the year compared to the first half and margin operators should be profitable," Dunford told the Canadian Wheat Board's annual Grain World conference.
The Canadian dollar and feed costs remain the big question marks for 1997 but exports are seen staying strong, she said.
CANFAX, part of the Canadian Cattlemen's Association, puts 1998 Canadian beef production at 3.05 billion lbs, 1999 at 2.955 billion lbs, and 2000 output at 2.866 billion lbs.

"In 1998, production will still be large but prices begin a recovery," Dunford said. "For 1999 to 2000, cattle numbers will be decreasing, production down, cattle prices improve considerably, and cow/calf profits improve," Dunford said.
Preliminary figures for 1996 put total beef exports at 46 percent of production, unchanged from 1995, while net exports as a percentage of production rose to 30 percent from 28 pct.

Preliminary data for 1996 put total beef exports to the United States at 274 million kg, up 28 percent from 214 million kg in 1995. Actual exports of Canadian live cattle to the U.S. in 1996 totalled 1.51 million head, up 34 percent from the 1.13 million exported in 1995, according to CANFAX.

Japan will remain a top customer for Canadian beef. CANFAX put Canadian beef exports to Japan at a preliminary 12 million kg (12,000 tonnes) in 1996, against 11.4 million kg (11,000 tonnes) a year earlier.
Total exports of Canadian beef to destinations other than the U.S. in 1996 were estimated at 14.4 million kg for all Asia including Japan, down from 15.4 million.
The drop in volume was largely due to a 30 percent decline in shipments to South Korea, according to CANFAX.
Shipments to the European Union in 1996 also fell sharply to 650,000 kg in 1996 from 2.061 million kg a year earlier. ((Winnipeg bureau, 204 947 3548))
